description: We are Star AI Lab's, a passionate team of engineers and researchers in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project, Lunar Landing Site Navigator, is an interactive, data-grounded 3D platform designed to explore and evaluate lunar landing destinations. By fusing verified NASA planetary data with modern spatial computing and intelligent analysis, we make complex space science intuitive and accessible for the future of lunar exploration.
summary:
SELENARA X is an advanced interactive 3D Lunar Landing Site Navigator and Mission Planning Workbench developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Landing safely on the Moon requires navigating unforgiving terrain hazards, ensuring uninterrupted direct-to-Earth communication, and maximizing solar power generation in extreme lighting environments. 

SELENARA X solves this multi-variable challenge by fusing authentic NASA open science—including LRO LOLA topography, NASA Moon Trek global imagery, and NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris—into an intuitive, browser-based 3D aerospace cockpit. Planners can evaluate high-priority candidate sites across the Moon (including polar craters like Mons Mouton and Shackleton), simulate localized terrain slope hazards, model hourly solar power budgets, and identify the optimal "Golden Landing Window" for mission survival. 

Additionally, SELENARA X features an event-anchored orbital Journey Engine tracking real NASA CLPS commercial missions (Intuitive Machines, Blue Ghost, Peregrine) and custom user-defined landing plans. By transforming complex orbital mechanics into accessible, real-time 3D intelligence, SELENARA X empowers scientists, students, and engineers to explore and plan the future of lunar exploration.
details:
1. What does it do & How does it work?

SELENARA X is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar landing site navigator and mission intelligence cockpit. It allows aerospace engineers, researchers, and space enthusiasts to visualize, evaluate, and plan lunar landing missions in full 3D.

The application integrates:

- 3D Interactive Lunar World: Built on Three.js and WebGL, rendering high-resolution lunar surface topography and authentic orbital perspective from Earth to Moon.

- Topographic & Hazard Evaluation: Uses NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation datasets to calculate terrain slope angles and crater depth hazards at any latitude/longitude coordinate.

- Ephemeris & Illumination Engine: Computes precise Sun and Earth elevation angles above the local lunar horizon over time, grounded by analytical celestial models and NASA JPL Horizons API queries.

- Power Budget Simulation: Models lander battery state-of-charge, solar panel collection efficiency, and thermal degradation through the extreme lunar day/night cycle.

- CLPS Flight Profile Trajectories: Reconstructs the end-to-end flight trajectories of real Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) missions (including IM-1 Odysseus, Blue Ghost Mission 1, and Peregrine) using published mission anchors.

---

2. What benefits does it have & What is the intended impact?

Landing on the lunar surface—especially near the resource-rich South Pole—is fraught with peril due to elongated shadows, extreme temperature shifts, and rough terrain. SELENARA X delivers:

- Rapid Multi-Criteria Decision Making: Instead of consulting disparate spreadsheets and static maps, planners can evaluate slope safety, communication line-of-sight to Earth, and solar energy in a unified interface.

- Golden Landing Window Identification: The system calculates the ideal touchdown epochs where solar elevation is high enough for power but shallow enough to reveal crater hazards via contrast shadows.

- Democratizing Space Science: By running entirely in the browser with zero software installation, SELENARA X bridges complex orbital physics and public education, inspiring the Artemis generation.

---

3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei), TanStack Query, Zustand.

- Backend Architecture: Fastify (Node.js), TypeScript, Vercel Serverless Functions.

- Research & Physics Engine: Python 3 (NumPy, SciPy, Pillow) for astronomical ephemeris algorithms, Meeus celestial mechanics, and digital elevation models (DEM).

- Deployment & Hosting: Vercel Global Edge Network with CDN-cached 3D binary assets (.glb).

- NASA Data Systems: NASA LRO LOLA, NASA Solar System Treks (Moon Trek), NASA JPL Horizons, and LROC QuickMap.

---

4. How is your project creative?

Rather than presenting lunar exploration as a static 2D map, SELENARA X creates an immersive mission-control cockpit. It features an interactive Guided Mission Tour, real-time coordinate transformations, an AI Mission Copilot providing grounded mission intelligence, and the ability to test custom lander presets (from 100 kg micro-landers to heavy cargo classes) under realistic lunar conditions.

---

5. What factors did your team consider?

- Extreme Polar Lighting: Near 85°–90° South, shadows can stretch dozens of kilometers. Our horizon calculation accounts for terrain obscuration to prevent missions from landing in permanent shadow traps.

- Communication Blackouts: Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication requires unblocked line-of-sight to Earth, which wobbles due to lunar libration. SELENARA X tracks sub-Earth coordinates to predict communication loss.

- Scientific Integrity & Open Science: Every dataset, calculation anchor, and 3D spacecraft model is transparently attributed to official NASA and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) sources without fabricating speculative telemetry.
